finding.claim: A request with Content-Type 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=utf-8' never selects the urlencoded body processor, so the body is not parsed into ARGS_POST or REQUEST_BODY and phase-2 rules see no body data (WAF bypass; conditional on the deployed rule set not re-selecting the processor, and on SecRequestBodyAccess being On).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request header Content-Type with a parameter suffix, plus a malicious form-encoded body (transaction.go:376 AddRequestHeader).
finding.sink: Phase-2 rule evaluation over ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY (transaction.go:1116-1119 empty-processor branch).

trace.note: AddRequestHeader receives the Content-Type header
value is lowercased
exact string compare with application/x-www-form-urlencoded fails due to the parameter suffix, so reqbodyProcessor is not set
ProcessRequestBody proceeds because the body is non-empty
MIME is read with parameters intact, inconsistent with line 386
rbp is empty
ForceRequestBodyVariable is false by default (waf.go:210), so no URLENCODED fallback
empty rbp branch evaluates PhaseRequestBody rules without parsing the body

finding.guards_checked: ForceRequestBodyVariable default false (waf.go:210); the only other writer of reqbodyProcessor is ctl:requestBodyProcessor (transaction.go:1113), which requires a rule to re-select; RequestBodyAccess defaults to false (waf.go:330), so exploitation requires SecRequestBodyAccess On. Not verified: whether the CRS rule set re-selects the processor for form content types regardless of parameters.

finding.claim: Duplicate Content-Type headers are resolved differently at header time (last matching value sets the processor) and at body time (first value is used as the MIME), so a multipart body can be parsed as urlencoded and its fields never reach ARGS_POST (conditional on the backend using the other header value).
finding.source: Two Content-Type request headers: 'multipart/form-data; boundary=X' followed by 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'.

trace.note: second header sets reqbodyProcessor to URLENCODED (last match wins)
mimeType is taken as m[0], the first Content-Type value (multipart/form-data)
urlencoded parser ignores the MIME and splits the multipart bytes on '&', so real form fields never appear in ARGS_POST

finding.guards_checked: No normalization or rejection of duplicate Content-Type headers in the library. Exploitation depends on the downstream backend selecting the other header value. Confidence medium.

finding.claim: Query arguments beyond WAF.ArgumentLimit (default 1000) are dropped silently, and which keys are dropped is randomized by Go map iteration, so an attacker can make an injected argument uninspected with high probability by sending many unique junk keys.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled query string with more than 1000 unique keys, with the payload in one of them.
finding.sink: ARGS_GET population used by argument-targeted rules.

trace.note: doParseQuery builds a Go map of key to values
each key is stored in the map, so iteration order is randomized
ExtractGetArguments ranges over the map
AddGetRequestArgument calls checkArgumentLimit before each add
over-limit argument is skipped with only a debug-logger warning; no variable or flag is set
checkArgumentLimit compares Len() (unique key count, collections/named.go:58-59) against ArgumentLimit

finding.guards_checked: ArgumentLimit default 1000 (waf.go:348). No rule-visible flag for the drop. Body arguments are not subject to the limit: bodyprocessors/urlencoded.go:27-30 writes ArgsPost directly, so the query and body paths are inconsistent. The raw query remains visible in REQUEST_URI, so only argument-targeted rules are bypassed.

finding.claim: A request target with an invalid percent-escape in the path (for example '/x%zz?q=<payload>') makes url.ParseRequestURI fail, and the query string is then never extracted into ARGS_GET; the fallback that would do so is commented out (connector-dependent: Go net/http rejects such targets upstream).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled raw request target containing an invalid percent-escape in the path, with the payload in the query.

trace.note: url.ParseRequestURI fails on the invalid escape
urlencodedError is set; only effective if a rule checks URLENCODED_ERROR
whole URI, including the query, is stored as the path
commented-out fallback that would extract the query is disabled
ExtractGetArguments is only reached on the success path, so ARGS_GET stays empty

finding.guards_checked: URLENCODED_ERROR flag, which helps only if a rule inspects it. Go net/http rejects invalid targets before the WAF, so exploitability depends on the connector forwarding raw request targets.

finding.claim: When io.Copy fails with a non-EOF error while writing a multipart file part, the function returns before the temp file is registered in filesTmpNames, so Transaction.Close never removes it and uploaded content persists in UploadDir.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled multipart file part whose body read fails with an error other than io.ErrUnexpectedEOF.
finding.sink: Temporary file left in UploadDir (disk, with retained uploaded content).

trace.note: os.CreateTemp creates the file in storagePath
io.Copy writes the part body into the temp file
non-EOF error sets MultipartStrictError and returns err
filesTmpNamesCol.Add is never reached for this file
Close removes only files registered in filesTmpNames, so the orphan survives

finding.guards_checked: Temp file name is random via os.CreateTemp and the client filename is not used in a path (multipart.go:58-64), so there is no traversal. The trigger condition is narrow and was not enumerated. Retention concern under the org policy on customer data.

finding.claim: Repeated multipart filenames overwrite the FILES_SIZES entry, because SetIndex(filename, 0, size) replaces index 0 for an existing key, so a size rule keyed on FILES_SIZES can be evaded while FILES_COMBINED_SIZE still reflects the true total.
finding.source: Two file parts with the same filename, the first large and the second small.
finding.sink: FILES_SIZES values consumed by size-limit rules.

trace.note: filesCol.Add records the filename for each file part
fileSizesCol.SetIndex(filename, 0, size) overwrites the existing size for that filename
SetIndex places the value at the index, replacing the existing entry
FILES_COMBINED_SIZE is computed from a running total and is correct

finding.guards_checked: No duplicate-filename detection in the multipart processor. Impact limited to size-based rules that read FILES_SIZES.
